source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Plant Growth and Development
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Primary growth in length of a stem is produced mainly by the
questions.explanation: Shoot and root apical meristems add cells at the tips and elongate the axis.

questions.stem: The exponential (log) phase of a sigmoid growth curve is the phase of
questions.explanation: After a lag, cells divide and expand rapidly; later the curve levels into a stationary phase.

questions.stem: Formation of interfascicular cambium from parenchyma is an example of
questions.explanation: Living differentiated cells regain meristematic activity (dedifferentiation) to form cambium.

questions.stem: Apical dominance is maintained chiefly by
questions.explanation: IAA from the terminal bud suppresses axillary buds; removing the tip releases them.

questions.stem: Bolting of rosette plants is promoted by
questions.explanation: GA stretches internodes so a rosette shoots up and flowers (bolting).

questions.stem: Cytokinins are best known for promoting
questions.explanation: Cytokinins (kinetin, zeatin) stimulate cytokinesis and are used in tissue culture with auxin.

questions.stem: The gaseous PGR that promotes fruit ripening is
questions.explanation: Ethylene is the ripening hormone of climacteric fruits such as banana and tomato.

questions.stem: Closure of stomata during water stress is induced by
questions.explanation: ABA is the stress hormone that closes stomata and also helps impose seed dormancy.

questions.stem: The plant organ that perceives photoperiod for flowering is the
questions.explanation: Leaves measure day/night length; a floral stimulus then moves to the shoot apex.

questions.stem: Vernalisation is the promotion of flowering by
questions.explanation: A chilling treatment of the seedling or soaked seed induces flowering in winter cereals and biennials.

questions.stem: Which is a synthetic auxin used as a herbicide?
questions.explanation: 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid kills broad-leaved weeds and is also used to induce parthenocarpy.

questions.stem: A short-day plant flowers when the photoperiod is
options: longer than a critical day length
shorter than a critical day length
questions.explanation: SDP (actually long-night plants) flower when the day is shorter than a critical length.

questions.stem: The triple response of etiolated seedlings to ethylene includes
options: longer roots, free elongation and no hook
inhibited elongation, stem swelling and an exaggerated hook
questions.explanation: Ethylene shortens and thickens the hypocotyl and tightens the apical hook.

questions.stem: Plant growth is said to be open or indeterminate because
questions.explanation: Apical and lateral meristems keep producing new cells, so the plant body has no fixed adult size.

questions.stem: The three phases of a sigmoid growth curve are
questions.explanation: Slow start (lag), exponential rise (log) and levelling (stationary) give the S-shaped curve.

questions.stem: Heterophylly in coriander or larkspur is an example of
questions.explanation: The same genotype makes different leaf shapes in air versus water or at different ages.

questions.stem: The principal natural auxin of higher plants is
questions.explanation: Went’s Avena test and later chemistry identified IAA as the main native auxin.

questions.stem: Foolish-seedling (bakanae) disease of rice led to the discovery of
questions.explanation: Gibberella fujikuroi infection overproduced GA and made rice seedlings elongate wildly.

questions.stem: The natural cytokinin first obtained from maize grains is
questions.explanation: Zeatin was isolated from Zea mays; kinetin was first obtained from herring-sperm DNA.

questions.stem: Which PGR is used to initiate flowering and synchronise fruit set in pineapple?
questions.explanation: Ethylene (or ethephon) induces pineapple flowering and can also promote female flowers in cucumber.

questions.stem: Seed dormancy is often maintained by high levels of
questions.explanation: ABA keeps the embryo quiescent; GA later antagonises ABA and promotes germination.

questions.stem: Phytochrome exists in two interconvertible forms known as
questions.explanation: Red light converts Pr to Pfr; far-red converts Pfr back to Pr and can cancel a long-night interruption.

questions.stem: Which statement about seed dormancy is incorrect?
options: A hard seed coat can impose dormancy
Vernalisation always means boiling the seed
questions.explanation: Vernalisation is a cold treatment for flowering, not boiling; heat/scarification are other dormancy-breaking methods.

questions.stem: Cytokinins delay senescence of leaves mainly by
options: preventing nutrient mobilisation out of the leaf
questions.explanation: They keep the leaf a nutrient sink, so chlorophyll and protein persist longer (Richmond–Lang effect).

questions.stem: Which plant is a classical short-day (long-night) example?
questions.explanation: Xanthium, soybean and chrysanthemum are SDP; spinach, radish and sugar beet are long-day plants.

questions.stem: Which statement about cell-fate changes in plants is correct?
options: Cork cambium arises by dedifferentiation of cortex or parenchyma
questions.explanation: Cork cambium (phellogen) is a secondary meristem formed from differentiated living cells.
